_comment: Wheeled variants: controller bases, wheel drives, wheels and third supports. class: maker = maker's or distributor's own published figure; third-party = parts catalogue; assumed = not published, with the reason. Lengths in mm, masses in g, torque in N m.

geometry.note: Wheels on the rear axle line of the walker chassis, support post under the two shelf holes at x = 92. Wheels at the front is the same build with the head pinned on facing the other way and the drive reversed.

friction._comment: Coefficients against a hard indoor floor. No measured data for these pairs on laminate, tile or vinyl was found; all are assumed from generic tables and one vendor note, and the range is run as sensitivity.

rubber.why: LEGO tyres; generic tables give 0.5 to 0.9 for rubber on dry hard surfaces

o_ring.why: nitrile O-ring or a rubber band; same generic rubber figures

tpu.why: TPU 95A; one printer vendor's note gives 0.70 to 0.80 on hardwood with no method

tt_tyre.why: the stock TT tyre is a harder compound than a LEGO tyre

pla.why: bare printed PLA or PETG; generic tables give 0.3 to 0.35 for polystyrene on steel

skid.why: a printed PLA dome sliding on the floor

ball_in_cup.why: a ball in a plain printed cup does not roll freely: it slides in the cup, so its drag is the cup friction acting at the ball radius

rolling.why: rolling resistance of small tyres on a hard floor; generic tables give 0.01 to 0.02 for car tyres and note that small wheels are worse

ball.name: Ball in a printed cup (tip_ball_16p5 with a LEGO 16.5 mm ball, or tip_ball_12p7 with a 12.7 mm steel ball)
ball.note: The EV3 31313 set has three 16.5 mm balls (part 54821) and no ball caster. The steel caster ball 99948 is in the education set 45544 only. The 51515 set has neither.

idler.name: Printed idler with TPU tyre on a Technic axle (tip_idler_fork, idler_hub, idler_tyre_tpu)
idler.note: Fixed axis: it rolls straight ahead and scrubs sideways in a turn. Analysed for drag only, not simulated.

o_rings.standard: Metric sections 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3 and 5 mm; ISO 3601 and DIN 3771 use 1.80, 2.65, 3.55, 5.30 and 7.00 mm
o_rings.stretch: Installed stretch of 1 to 5 percent on the inner diameter, 2 percent ideal; the grooves use 2 percent
o_rings.groove: 3.4 mm wide, 2.0 mm deep, ring 1.0 mm proud; the ring sets the rolling diameter: 44.8, 57.0 and 65.2 mm
o_rings.band_groove: 7.0 mm wide, 0.5 mm deep: one rubber band up to 6 mm wide (size 64) or two 3 mm bands (size 33) side by side

hardness.value: 95A assumed; Ultimaker's TPU 95A data sheet gives 96 Shore A

tpu.design: tyre 4 mm thick, bore 2 percent under the hub (stretch), eight keys against slipping round, a 1 mm lip each side against walking off, plain extrusion so it prints without supports
tpu.printing: Print slowly: a maker of softer filament gives 15 to 35 mm/s. Direct-drive extruders cope better. Retraction settings vary by machine and are not given here. Softer TPU needs more stretch than 2 percent.

unoq_pwm.value: D3, D5, D6, D9, D10 and D11 are the pins the datasheet marks as PWM; all 3.3 V logic

braccio_pins.value: The Braccio shield uses exactly those six for its servos, and D12 for soft start

control.unoq_free: With the shield fitted the free pins are D2, D4, D7, D8, D13, D20, D21 and A0 to A5. None is marked PWM. D2, D7, D8, D13, D20 and D21 do carry timer channels in the datasheet's pin map (TIM2_CH2, TIM8_CH4N, TIM3_CH1, TIM1_CH1N, TIM2_CH4, TIM2_CH3), which matches the list reported for this project, but whether the Zephyr core gives PWM on them is not verified.
control.unoq_servo: A wheeled UNO Q does not use the Braccio servos, so the simplest wiring is the shield itself: plug the two 360-degree servos into two of its servo headers (D11 and D10) and let its 5 V supply feed them. Without the shield, use two of the marked PWM pins and the separate pack.
control.unoq_tt: TB6612FNG without the shield: PWMA D5, PWMB D6, AIN1 D2, AIN2 D4, BIN1 D7, BIN2 D8, STBY tied high. DRV8833: IN1 to IN4 on D5, D6, D9, D10.

pi_pwm.value: Two hardware PWM channels: PWM0 on GPIO12 or GPIO18, PWM1 on GPIO13 or GPIO19

control.pi_servo: Two servos fit the two hardware channels (GPIO12 and GPIO13). Software PWM from RPi.GPIO jitters; the pigpio daemon times pulses by DMA. A PCA9685 board (16 channels, 12 bit, I2C) is the alternative.
control.pi_tt: TB6612FNG: PWMA GPIO12, PWMB GPIO13, AIN1 GPIO5, AIN2 GPIO6, BIN1 GPIO20, BIN2 GPIO21, STBY GPIO16.

drivers.name: TB6612FNG
drivers.current: 1 A continuous, 3 A peak per channel
drivers.pins: PWM, IN1, IN2 per motor and a shared STBY
drivers.verdict: fits the TT motor at 6 V; its 1.5 A stall is inside the peak rating

drivers.name: DRV8833
drivers.current: 1.2 A continuous, 2 A peak per channel
drivers.pins: two inputs per motor, PWM on either
drivers.verdict: fits; fewest pins if four PWM outputs are free

drivers.name: L298N module
drivers.pins: IN1, IN2 and EN (PWM) per motor
drivers.verdict: drops 1.8 V typically and up to 3.2 V at 1 A: from 6 V the TT motor sees about 4 V. Avoid.

basex.value: Four LEGO motor ports with encoder registers (2 A in total), two servo outputs taking an angle or a 500 to 2500 pulse, I2C address 0x22, 9 to 12 V for motor power
